origin_derivations.TLS-7: SSL.listen/2 and SSL.handshake/3 normalize through ServerOptions.build/1, whose sni/1 is the only producer of {:fun, fun}: the caller :sni_fun, validated as arity one and exclusive with :sni_hosts. ListenSocket is opaque and built only by listen/2; transport_accept/2 passes its retained options to ServerConnection.start/3. The sole lookup/2 caller, select_identity/2, runs once for the first ClientHello and replaces only identity and signature_algorithms, retaining sni. The callback result is data: identity keyword options loaded by ClientIdentity.load/1 (TLS-2 password boundary); exceptions and invalid results become internal_error. No library producer supplies sni_fun; Hell forwards caller options. The user sni_fun body is the approved server callback boundary. rc.13 follow-up (8e810b4): lookup/3 now runs the callback in a monitored helper bounded by the handshake deadline; the invocation (181) moves into the helper closure body call_sni_fun/2 (194->262, expression fun.(name) unchanged). Its callable is the same caller :sni_fun that sni/1 validates and stores as {:fun, fun}; sni/1 remains the only producer and no library caller supplies one. rc.17 follow-up (055f9fb): the invocation (181) moves 262->266 in call_sni_fun/2 with fun.(name) unchanged; build/1 only adds the literal active_chunk_size/1 validation.
origin_derivations.TLS-4: PKIX.client_peer/3 (server mTLS) validates the client path against normalized trust anchors with a nil verifier and no hostname matcher. hostname_match_fun/3 is unchanged and moves 767->817.
origin_derivations.TLS-6: HandshakeCore still selects config.certificate_policy || &PKIX.peer/6 and only extracts the alert mapping into certificate_alert/1; verify_peer/3 moves 768->789. allow_early_data is a boolean handshake input.
origin_derivations.unchanged_sites: Server handshake, server flight, QUIC resumption/session and SSL.QUIC continuation bodies introduce no other unresolved dispatch, callback option or OTP SSL call; QUIC Config accepts only the data-valued :resumption policy.
